terms.gloss: of history, historical; (as a noun) a historian
evidence: Cic. Brut. 286: nōn tam historicō quam ōrātōriō genere
Cic. Mur. 16: hominēs litterātī et historicī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of history and of writing it: genus historicum, the historians’ style; fidēs historica, a historian’s credibility (Ov. Am. 3.12.42); of people, versed in history. As a noun, a historian (Cic. Top. 78; Quint.).

terms.gloss: in all recorded history, within human memory
terms.comment: Cicero’s way of saying “for the first time in history”; nostrā memoriā is “in our time” (Lewis & Short, s.v. memoria).

evidence: Plin. Ep. 2.5.5: nōn historicē tantum, sed prope poēticē (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: et eārum rērum historiam quae erant Athēnīs ipsīus aetāte gestae nōn tam historicō quam ōrātōriō genere perscrīpsit.
phrases.english: and he wrote the history of what had happened at Athens in his own lifetime in a style less historical than oratorical.

phrases.latin: sī hoc post hominum memoriam contigit nēminī
phrases.english: if this has happened to no one in all recorded history

sources: Lewis & Short: historicus · Lewis & Short: memoria
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 328.
